The wide, tall, early complex is beat 7.

Counting the sharp QRS spikes from the left, the peaks fall at roughly x ≈ 190, 261, 334, 406, 480, 550, 593, 694, and so on. The first six are evenly spaced at about 70–74 px apart, which is the sinus-like baseline rhythm. The beat at x ≈ 593 comes only about 43 px after the sixth beat, so it is premature. It is also much taller and broader than the surrounding narrow complexes. It is followed by a longer pause (about 101 px) before the next beat, consistent with a premature ventricular contraction.

FINAL ANSWER: 7
